clippings.speaker: Noah Baumbach
clippings.quote: We kind of just felt very in sync in writing it, to the point that we would even divvy up scenes and write them separately and then we’d send them back and forth and rework them together. But there was no danger in that because everything felt of the same piece — and I don’t know why that is except that we connected very strongly about the material and the character.
clippings.title: Flavorwire Interview: Greta Gerwig and Noah Baumbach on Creating ‘Frances Ha’ Together
clippings.context: Joint interview on the release of Frances Ha, their first co-written script.

clippings.speaker: Greta Gerwig
clippings.quote: And I’m so happy we got to do it together, because it felt like a really natural collaboration and I didn’t feel like either one of our voices was compromised in it. You know, though he’s clearly the more accomplished of the two writers, he was never like, ‘Which one of us have an Academy Award nomination and which one of us doesn’t?!’ Although he could have said that.
clippings.title: Flavorwire Interview: Greta Gerwig and Noah Baumbach on Creating ‘Frances Ha’ Together
clippings.context: Same Frances Ha interview, on co-writing with Baumbach after years of improvised films.

clippings.speaker: Greta Gerwig
clippings.quote: One thing I learned from my experience writing scripts with Noah Baumbach for two movies, is that he’s relentless about trying to get it right on the page, because you only answer to yourself during that period of time, so you can really make it as perfect as possible.
clippings.title: INTERVIEW: Greta Gerwig, Writer and Director of Lady Bird
clippings.context: Interview about her solo directing debut, explaining why she nails the script before shooting.

clippings.speaker: Noah Baumbach
clippings.quote: Then it was the most fun I think either of us have ever had, right? And then at a certain point, I was like, ‘I think this is the best thing we’ve ever written.’ I know enough always just to follow what Greta says, so even in my bellyaching and revolting, I kind of knew, ‘Well if she really believes it, then there’s something there.’
clippings.title: ‘Barbie’ Co-Writer Noah Baumbach Initially Thought Film Was a ‘Terrible Idea,’ but Greta Gerwig ‘Signed Me Up’: ‘You’ve Gotta Get Us Out of This’
clippings.context: WGA West Q&A moderated by Judd Apatow, Baumbach's first in-depth talk about Barbie after the strike.

clippings.speaker: Noah Baumbach
clippings.quote: Greta will go into some monologue mode, it's kind of almost physical. Like, she goes in and she just like-- and kind of like, (laugh) doing a thing and, like, you know, it's like Joe Cocker or something. (laugh) it's like -and then, she hands it over. And-- and it's great.
clippings.title: "Barbie" filmmaker Greta Gerwig says she "still can't believe anybody let me do this"
clippings.context: 60 Minutes transcript; Baumbach describing how Gerwig writes the soul-baring monologues in her films.

clippings.speaker: Greta Gerwig
clippings.quote: We hadn’t written together in a long time. Even when we’re not credited on each other’s stuff, we’re always looking at everything and giving feedback and talking all the time. But we hadn’t actually sat down and written something together. And in my heart, I felt, ‘It’s so fun to write together.’
clippings.title: Greta Gerwig Explains the Exhilarating Freedom of Imagining Her Hit ‘Barbie’
clippings.context: IndieWire Honors interview on why she signed Baumbach up to co-write Barbie.

notes: Fresh Air 2013 transcript had little direct talk about each other; PopMatters and moviemom Lady Bird lines were thinner, so I skipped them.
